company_name: New China Life Insurance Company Ltd.
model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run growth of the earning base, i.e. investment assets (+12.2% FY2025, +3.3% in H1 2026 to RMB1.90tn) and the CSM (181.7bn -> 193.9bn in H1 2026, +6.7%), cross-checked against GWP +6.9% in H1 2026 and EV +7.8% in six months; fades to 3% terminal. Revenue CAGRs are IFRS 17 artefacts, EPS CAGRs start from the FY2022 trough, and equity CAGRs are depressed by OCI; none is used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (2.7%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (54.6%) by far more than 30%: FY2022 EPS 3.15 was a market-trough year and FY2025 EPS 11.63 a peak year, while equity carries -24.4bn of FY2025 OCI and the IFRS 17 restatement. Revenue CAGRs are negative only because FY2020-22 are IFRS 4 premiums-based. The warning is noted and all three series are set aside in favour of the normalisation in inputs.notes.

scenario_narratives.base: A state-controlled pure-play Chinese life insurer whose 2023-25 reform delivered VNB +57% and EV +11%, valued on the dividends it can actually pay. Profit normalises from the FY2025 / H1 2026 market-rally peak to ~1.3% of a RMB2tn investment book (~RMB26-28bn), grows with the book and the CSM at 5% fading to 3%, and the payout climbs from 28% toward the peer-level 50% as capital consumption eases. Capitalised at a 10.5% CNY cost of equity with the terminal capped at 12x FCFE, the H-share is worth roughly 0.5x embedded value -- well above a price that currently discounts it at 0.36x EV, 0.9x IFRS book and ~3x peak earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: Investment yields hold near 5%, VNB compounds at 12-15%, the margin settles at 21-22% instead of 19%, solvency rebuilds and the payout reaches 55%; the H-share rerates toward the A-share's 0.8x EV.
scenario_narratives.bear: An H2 2026 equity drawdown and a further CGB yield decline expose negative-spread risk on the legacy guaranteed book; profit falls to the FY2022-23 level, the payout stays at 25-30% to protect a core solvency ratio drifting toward 110%, and the stock settles at 9x a flat dividend stream -- below today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a Chinese life insurer on the cash it distributes, not on IFRS 17 net income (dominated by FVTPL and OCI investment variance) and not on OCF (policyholder float). Profit before tax after the structurally low 13.5% effective rate is the earnings measure; the payout ratio, calibrated to the FY2025 dividend and the H1 2026 solvency trajectory, sets how much of it must be retained. Debt interest is inside that measure, so net debt is zero. The FY2025 and H1 2026 margins are peak-cycle and are normalised down to the FY2019-25 average profit/investment-assets ratio, which coincides with the ~RMB29bn steady-state earnings the company's own embedded-value framework implies. CROSS-CHECK against EV: the base value of ~RMB50/share is ~0.5x the H1 2026 EV of RMB99.5/share (310,384 / 3,119.5) and the bull ~0.8x; the current H-share price is 0.36x EV, the A-share 0.53x. A full appraisal value (EV + 5x VNB = ~RMB120/share) is not used because the EV's 4.0% investment-return assumption sits 220bp above the 10-year CGB and the market has, reasonably, never paid it for an H-share lifer. Retained earnings are charged as lost cash (the engine's retention plug), which understates value if retained capital genuinely compounds EV at the 8.5% RDR; the rising payout path is the compromise, and its sensitivity is stated in inputs.notes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital-markets leverage: ~21% of a RMB1.9tn investment book in equities/funds and 31.5% at FVTPL; a 10% A-share drawdown is roughly a year of normalised profit through P&L and OCI
Negative-spread risk: 10-year CGB yield ~1.8% and net investment yield 2.6% (H1 2026) against a legacy book with 3-3.5% guarantees; the EV's 4.0% long-run return assumption may be too high

Regulatory repricing: NFRA illustrated-rate cap cut 3.9% -> 3.5% from 1 July 2026 and guaranteed-rate cuts compress new-business margins industry-wide; participating products also consume more capital

Solvency trajectory: core solvency fell from 135.11% to 126.21% in H1 2026 despite RMB22.8bn of profit; a further fall would cap the payout path the valuation depends on (payout flat at 25% roughly halves the base value)
Payout policy is a state-shareholder decision (Central Huijin, China Baowu); the rise to 50% is a judgment, not guidance
A/H structure: the H-share has traded at a 30%+ discount to the A-share for years; the model values the H at the H price but there is no mechanism forcing convergence
Q3 2026 results (c. 29 Oct 2026) are the first evidence on H2 2026; the base assumes a weak H2 and the bear an H2 loss -- an H2 as strong as H1 would move the FY2026 anchor up ~RMB14bn of PBT
Model risk: FCFE charges all retained earnings as lost; if retained capital compounds EV at the RDR, value is understated by a wide margin

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 41.88-65.80. FX: Yahoo HKDCNY=X, inverted, same date; A-share parity from 601336.SS
data_sources.financials: 1336.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, RMB millions, FY2016-FY2025 + H1 FY2023-FY2026); FY2025 Annual Report (consolidated income statement, investment income table, embedded value section incl. ANW/VIF/VNB, solvency, dividends, borrowings, Note 8 leases); H1 2026 Interim Report (share capital table, EV 310,384 / VNB 6,916, solvency 126.21% / 195.74%, investment assets 1,901,854 and yields, CSM 193,857, equity 123,578, tax)
data_sources.qualitative: 1336.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-16): reform program, EV/VNB disclosure, product-mix shift, NFRA rate cuts, solvency, bull/bear cases

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues as the CSV defines them (FY2025 AR consolidated income statement line 'Total revenues' 155,551): insurance revenue 50,297 + investment income 104,582 (= net investment income 46,058 + realized gains 37,373 + fair value gains 22,121 + associates 2,255 less impairment 3,473, plus other) + other income. The IFRS 17 top line is NOT premiums: GWP was 195,871 in FY2025 (+14.9%) and 129,570 in H1 2026 (+6.9%). About 60bn of the FY2025 figure is realized and fair-value gains earned in a strong A-share year, which is why the pre-tax margin path normalises DOWN from the FY2025 level rather than being carried forward. H1 2026 total revenues 81,554 vs 69,429 (+17.5%); H2 2025 was 86,122.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,119,546,600 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim report share capital table: 2,085,439,340 A shares 66.85% + 1,034,107,260 H shares 33.15%), unchanged since 2011. No share-based payment scheme, no convertibles, no treasury shares: basic = diluted (FY2025 AR weighted average 3,120M both years). A and H shares rank pari passu for dividends, so the per-share value is on the total count and the H-share price is compared against it. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the banks/insurers convention in this folder (LGEN.L, PRU, GL, 0998.HK). Borrowings RMB20,228M at 30 June 2026 are capital supplementary bonds (Tier 2 regulatory capital; 30,384 at FY2024 -> 20,173 at FY2025 after a redemption), whose coupon is deducted inside profit before tax, so the flows already pay for them. Repo financing is investment-operations funding and is excluded by the parser. Cash 33,065 is policyholder and investment-portfolio liquidity inside RMB1.90tn of investment assets, not shareholder surplus. Solvency surplus (comprehensive 195.74%, core 126.21% at 30 June 2026, down from 210.47% / 135.11% at FY2025) is the regulatory buffer that lets the company write participating business and is NOT added back.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 dividends declared, RMB8,516M = RMB2.73/share (interim 0.67 + final 2.06) x 3,119.5M shares, 23.5% of attributable net profit of 36,284 (FY2025 AR). This is the observed FCFE: the only cash a shareholder of a Chinese life insurer receives, and the realistic measure of distributable capital given that core solvency FELL from 135.11% to 126.21% in H1 2026 despite RMB22.8bn of profit (participating-product capital consumption and OCI movements under C-ROSS II). An insurer's OCF-less-capex (CSV 109,434 for FY2025) is policyholder premium float being invested, not free cash, so the identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied; reported_fcf is retained for auditability only.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report: no share-based payment, share option or share incentive scheme disclosed (grep of 'share-based payment', 'share option scheme', 'share incentive', 'equity-settled' returns nothing). State-controlled (Central Huijin) H/A-share insurer; SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks in any year of the history; the count has been 3,119.5M since the 2011 IPO. The flat count is a fact, not a modelling convention that needs funding.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are RMB (CNY) millions; the HKEX H-share quote is HKD. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 CNY = 1.1745 HKD, from Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8514 on 2026-10-16T08:01Z (inverted). Parity check against the Shanghai A-share (601336.SS, same economic rights): RMB52.31 x 1.1745 = HKD61.44 against the observed H-share HKD42.10, i.e. the H trades at a 31.5% discount to the A (AH premium ~46%). That gap is the structural A/H discount Chinese insurers carry (NCI's has historically been among the widest), so the check proves the rate's direction and magnitude, not price parity. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted; canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are HKD, comparable to current_price, with *_cny siblings. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday, 16:08 HKT); 52-week range 41.88-65.80, i.e. the price sits at the bottom of its range, 36% below the high, ahead of Q3 2026 results due around 29 October 2026
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.5%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% (mid-2026, approximate; no live CGB quote through the Yahoo chart endpoint) + beta ~1.3 x 6.5% China ERP = ~10.3%, rounded to 10.5%. The beta sits above a Chinese bank's because NCI's IFRS 17/9 earnings are the most capital-markets-levered of the big four life insurers (31.5% of investment assets at FVTPL, ~21% in equities and funds; comprehensive investment yield 8.5% -> 5.0% -> 6.4% across FY2024/FY2025/H1 2026). The low risk-free rate does NOT pull the CoE below the folder's other insurers (LGEN.L 10.5% GBP, PRU 10.0% USD, 0998.HK 10.5% CNY) because China's ERP is wider and the A/H structure adds a governance and capital-controls premium that H-share investors demonstrably price. One rate across all three scenarios; cyclicality and spread risk are carried in the bear path and its 30% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities RMB627M at FY2025 (FY2025 AR Note 8) against RMB1.9tn of assets; the IFRS 16 charge sits inside operating expenses already deducted in profit before tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are RMB34M of equity (H1 2026) and ~RMB5M of profit (FY2025: PBT 40,525 - tax 4,236 = 36,289 vs attributable 36,284). The cash-flow line 'non-controlling interests (25,580)' is third-party units in consolidated investment funds, not corporate NCI. Flows are modelled on profit before tax, which ties to attributable profit after tax within RMB5M, so no deduction is made.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a Chinese life insurer, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the LGEN.L / PRU / GL / IAG.AX pattern in this folder (SKILL.md routing row: insurer). Not the owner-FCF DCF: OCF of RMB56-111bn a year is policyholder premium float, and EBITDA does not exist. Not the routing table's default BVPS x exit-P/B either: IFRS 17 shareholders' equity (RMB123.6bn at H1 2026, 0.9x the H-share market cap) understates where the value sits -- the CSM store of future profit is RMB193.9bn and embedded value is RMB310.4bn -- and equity swings with OCI (FY2025 OCI -24.4bn after +36.0bn in FY2024). An EV/appraisal-value model is not an established route in this folder, so EV and VNB are used as the CROSS-CHECK and the normalisation anchor, not the engine (see valuation_philosophy). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenues as the CSV defines them (insurance revenue + investment income + other); ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax as % of revenue (FY2025 26.05%, FY2024 21.3%, FY2023 7.6%, H1 2026 32.6%; three-year FY2023-25 pooled 20.6%); sbc_pct_path = 0 (SBC-zero SOE); da = 0 (D&A ~1.8bn is inside the expense base); cash_tax_rate = 13.5% (FY2025 ETR 10.45%, H1 2026 14.4%, FY2024 a credit, FY2023 58% -- the low rate is structural: tax-exempt CGB interest and dividend income); capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = the share of after-tax profit kept as solvency capital and new-business strain, so FCFE = after-tax profit x payout ratio, with capex_pct = margin x (1 - tax) x (1 - payout). NORMALISATION: FY2025 and H1 2026 are peak-cycle (A-share rally: realized + FV gains 59.5bn in FY2025; annualised total investment yield 6.7% in H1 2026 vs the EV's own 4.0% long-run assumption and a 2.6% net investment yield). Attributable profit / average investment assets ran 1.8% (FY2019), 1.5%, 1.4%, 0.84%, 0.67% (FY2023), 1.75%, 2.07% (FY2025): the FY2019-25 mean is 1.44%, and the base path settles at ~1.3% of a ~2.1tn book by FY2028 (NI ~27-28bn, EPS ~RMB8.8), which is also what the EV framework implies for steady-state earnings (expected return on EV = ANW 227bn x 4.0% + VIF 83bn x 8.5% = ~16bn, plus VNB ~13bn annualised = ~29bn). PAYOUT: 23.5% in FY2025 is the lowest of the big four (China Life ~35%, Ping An ~40%+, CPIC ~35%); the base lifts it from 28% to 50% over ten years as reform-era capital consumption eases and the SOE market-value-management push continues (dividend +7.9% FY2025, interim +9.0% H1 2026, third consecutive year of interims). This payout path is the single largest judgment in the model: held flat at 25% the base value roughly halves. H2 2026 is NOT extrapolated from H1: the share price has fallen 36% from its 52-week high ahead of the Q3 2026 release, so the base assumes H2 2026 PBT of ~10-11bn (vs H1 26.6bn, H2 2025 24.3bn), i.e. a weak H2 market, and the bear assumes an H2 loss.
inputs.transition_note: FY2022 and earlier rows are IFRS 4 / IAS 39; FY2023 onward are IFRS 17 / IFRS 9 (FY2022 revenue 209,481 vs FY2023 72,254 is the presentation break, not an operating collapse). Equity FY2022 102,884 vs FY2023 105,067 straddles the restatement. No series spanning FY2022 is used as an anchor; the base is FY2025 and the H1 2026 run-rate, with the profit/investment-assets ratio (which is comparable across regimes) as the normalisation gauge.

bear.narrative: An H2 2026 A-share drawdown turns FVTPL gains into losses: FY2026 revenue -2%, margin 17% (PBT ~25.9bn, meaning an H2 loss of ~0.7bn after the 26.6bn H1 -- the FY2023 shape). FY2027: the 10-year CGB slides toward 1.5%, the 3.9% -> 3.5% illustrated-rate cap and 2.0% guaranteed-rate cuts cannot reprice the legacy 3-3.5% guaranteed book fast enough, and the negative-spread risk the whole industry carries shows up as a 13% margin (NI ~16.7bn, 0.8% of investment assets, the FY2022 level). Growth 2-3% thereafter as bancassurance single-premium volumes fall away. Core solvency slips toward 110%, so the payout is held at 25-30% until FY2030 and only reaches 40% by FY2035. Tax 15%. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/2.5%, 9x FCFE) -- the H-share stays at ~0.25x embedded value.

base.narrative: FY2026: revenue +4% (H1 +17.5% on the A-share rally; H2 assumed weak against a strong H2 2025, consistent with the 36% share-price fall into the Q3 release) at a 23.0% pre-tax margin = PBT ~37.2bn (H1 26.6bn + H2 ~10.6bn), attributable NI ~32.2bn after 13.5% tax, dividend ~9.0bn (+6%, payout 28%). FY2027: revenue flat (+1%) and margin normalises to 18.5% as realized/FV gains revert toward the EV's 4.0% long-run return: PBT ~30.2bn, NI ~26.1bn -- the through-cycle level of ~1.3% of investment assets. FY2028 onward: revenue +5-5.5% with the investment book and CSM (participating-product mix, bancassurance regular premium, 'five priorities' asset growth), margin 18.8-19.0%, growth fading to 3% by FY2035. Payout rises 2-3pp a year from 28% to 50% as the reform-era capital consumption eases and NCI closes the gap to peers. Tax 13.5%. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/3%, 12x FCFE = 6x earnings at a 50% payout) -- the cap binds, at the upper end of where Chinese H-share life insurers have traded on earnings.

bull.narrative: H2 2026 markets hold: FY2026 revenue +8%, margin 25% (NI ~36bn, in line with FY2025), then the investment yield settles at ~5% rather than 4% (equity allocation under the 'five priorities' mandates earns its keep, CGB yields stabilise), VNB keeps compounding 12-15% a year on the participating-product shift and bancassurance regular premium so CSM release grows faster than the book, and the margin normalises only to 21-22%. Core solvency rebuilds above 140% and the SOE market-value-management push takes the payout to 55% by FY2035. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/3.5%, 14x FCFE) -- a rerating to ~0.8x embedded value, where the A-share already trades.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the earnings base is the most capital-markets-levered of the big four (comprehensive investment yield 8.5% -> 5.0% -> 6.4% in 18 months), core solvency fell 9pp in H1 2026 despite record profit, the NFRA's illustrated-rate cut took effect 1 July 2026 and the 36% share-price fall into the Q3 2026 release says the market expects a weak H2 -- the bear axis is live, not hypothetical. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs a sustained ~5% investment yield, continued double-digit VNB growth, a doubling of the payout ratio and an A/H rerating all at once. 30/50/20 sits one notch more bearish than the 25/50/25 used for LGEN.L, PRU and 0998.HK, reflecting the single-market, single-regulator exposure.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
